req.title: Basic-auth accepts correct credentials
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> with HTTP 200 and an authenticated=true JSON body when the supplied Basic credentials match.

doc.reasoning: The basic_auth handler calls check_basic_auth(user, passwd) which inspects request.authorization. Key mutation targets: (1) the boolean check `not check_basic_auth(...)` — flipping to `check_basic_auth(...)` would return 401 on correct creds; (2) the exact status codes 200 vs 401; (3) the JSON body fields `authenticated=True` and `user=user`; (4) the credential comparison `auth.username == user and auth.password == passwd` — `and` vs `or`, `==` vs `!=`. Tests cover: correct credentials (EP positive), wrong password (NEG), wrong username (NEG), no credentials (NEG/BVA), special-character credentials (BVA), and the exact body field values (mutation-resilient assertions on both `authenticated` and `user`).

tests.name: test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200_and_body
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Client sends GET /basic-auth/alice/secret with Authorization: Basic base64(alice:secret)
actions: Build Basic auth header for alice:secret
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()
creds = base64.b64encode(b'alice:secret').decode('ascii')
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}

def test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200_and_body():
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/alice/secret', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'alice'
    assert len(data) == 2

tests.name: test_basic_auth_user_field_matches_path_param_not_credential_username
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Path param user and credential username are both 'testuser'
actions: Build Basic auth header for testuser:mypass
Assert user field in response equals path param 'testuser'
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

def test_basic_auth_user_field_matches_path_param_not_credential_username():
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'testuser:mypass').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/testuser/mypass', headers={'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'testuser'
    assert data['user'] != 'alice'

tests.name: test_basic_auth_special_chars_in_credentials
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Username and password contain special characters
actions: Build Basic auth header for user 'admin' and password 'p@ss!1'
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

def test_basic_auth_special_chars_in_credentials():
    passwd = 'p@ss!1'
    creds = base64.b64encode(f'admin:{passwd}'.encode()).decode('ascii')
    r = client.get(f'/basic-auth/admin/{passwd}', headers={'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'admin'

tests.name: test_basic_auth_response_body_has_exactly_two_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Correct credentials supplied
actions: Assert response body has exactly the keys 'authenticated' and 'user'
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

def test_basic_auth_response_body_has_exactly_two_keys():
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'myuser:mypass').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/myuser/mypass', headers={'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert set(data.keys()) == {'authenticated', 'user'}
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'myuser'
